matches.candidate_construct: SLC19A2 encodes the high-affinity thiamine transporter THTR1; loss reduces cellular thiamine uptake
matches.canonical_construct: Riboflavin transporter loss reduces intracellular riboflavin available for conversion to FMN and FAD
matches.canonical_vignette: A 9-year-old girl has progressive sensorineural hearing loss, gait ataxia, distal weakness, and bulbar dysfunction. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC52A2. An abnormal acylcarnitine profile improves after high-dose riboflavin therapy.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which intracellular consequence most directly links the transporter defect to impaired mitochondrial metabolism?

canonical_options.A: Reduced biotin availability for biotin-dependent carboxylases
canonical_options.B: Reduced formation of FMN and FAD cofactors used in oxidation-reduction reactions
canonical_options.C: Reduced synthesis of thiamine pyrophosphate for oxidative decarboxylation
canonical_options.D: Reduced formation of tetrahydrofolate one-carbon carriers
canonical_options.E: Reduced generation of adenosylcobalamin for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase

matches.candidate_construct: ETHE1 is a mitochondrial sulfur dioxygenase; its loss causes sulfide accumulation that inhibits cytochrome c oxidase
matches.canonical_construct: Primary LHON-causing mitochondrial DNA variants commonly affect MT-ND genes encoding subunits of respiratory-chain complex I, impairing NADH-to-ubiquinone electron transfer and mitochondrial ATP production in vulnerable retinal ganglion cells.
matches.canonical_vignette: A 23-year-old man develops painless blurring of central vision in one eye followed several weeks later by similar visual loss in the other eye. Visual field testing shows dense central scotomas. His mother is unaffected, but two maternal uncles developed comparable vision loss as young adults.
matches.canonical_lead_in: The most common pathogenic variants causing this disorder affect mitochondrial genes encoding subunits of which respiratory-chain complex?

matches.candidate_construct: SLC39A8 deficiency causes manganese deficiency, reducing activity of manganese-dependent Golgi beta-1,4-galactosyltransferase
matches.canonical_construct: PMM2 encodes phosphomannomutase 2, which converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate. Loss of PMM2 lowers the mannose-1-phosphate/GDP-mannose pool and impairs synthesis of lipid-linked oligosaccharides required for N-linked protein glycosylation.
matches.canonical_vignette: An infant has hypotonia, developmental delay, esotropia, inverted nipples, abnormal suprapubic fat pads, and cerebellar hypoplasia. Serum transferrin glycoform analysis suggests a congenital disorder of N-linked glycosylation, and genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in PMM2.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which metabolic conversion is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Mannose-6-phosphate tagging of lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi apparatus
canonical_options.C: Fructose-1-phosphate to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde

matches.candidate_construct: AGK is a kinase-independent subunit of the TIM22 complex required for import and assembly of mitochondrial carrier proteins
matches.canonical_construct: Citrin is the mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier that exports aspartate to the cytosol while importing glutamate plus a proton
matches.canonical_vignette: A 27-year-old man has recurrent episodes of confusion after carbohydrate-rich meals. During an episode, plasma ammonia and citrulline are markedly elevated. He has a longstanding preference for protein- and fat-rich foods. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A13.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which mitochondrial transport process is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
canonical_options.B: Export of aspartate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for glutamate plus a proton
canonical_options.C: Export of citrate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for malate
canonical_options.D: Import of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
canonical_options.E: Exchange of cytosolic ADP for mitochondrial ATP across the inner mitochondrial membrane

matches.candidate_construct: PANK2 is a pantothenate kinase that phosphorylates pantothenate at the entry step of coenzyme A biosynthesis
matches.canonical_construct: APRT is a cytoplasmic purine-salvage enzyme that uses adenine and phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate to synthesize AMP. APRT loss diverts adenine toward oxidation to poorly soluble 2,8-dihydroxyadenine, causing radiolucent kidney stones and crystal nephropathy.
matches.canonical_vignette: A 15-year-old adolescent has recurrent radiolucent kidney stones and progressive kidney dysfunction. Urine microscopy shows characteristic brown, round crystals, and stone analysis identifies 2,8-dihydroxyadenine. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in APRT.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which metabolic reaction is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Conversion of hypoxanthine and phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate to inosine monophosphate
canonical_options.C: Conversion of orotic acid and phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate to orotidine monophosphate
canonical_options.D: Conversion of adenine and phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate to adenosine monophosphate
